articles.title: In 1912, the German meteorologist Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents of the Earth had once been joined and were slowly drifting apart — a theory geologists ridiculed for the next 50 years, until three decades after his death, when new evidence from the ocean floor proved him right
articles.summary: In 1912, German meteorologist Alfred Wegener introduced his revolutionary theory of continental drift to the Frankfurt Geological Association. Originally an astronomer, Wegener proposed that continents slowly shift across the Earth's surface over vast geological periods. This groundbreaking idea, though initially controversial, profoundly influenced Earth sciences, eventually forming the bedrock for modern plate tectonics and our understanding of global geological dynamics.
